question:
Suppose that \(x\) and \(y\) are nonzero real numbers such that

\[\frac{3x + y}{x - 3y} = -2.\]

What is the value of \[\frac{x + 3y}{3x - y}?\]
solution:
Clearing the denominator reveals a useful relation between \(x\) and \(y\). The given fraction is defined, so we can multiply by \(x-3y\) to obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
3x+y&=-2(x-3y),\\
3x+y&=-2x+6y,\\
5x&=5y,\\
x&=y.
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting this relation into the requested expression gives
\[
\frac{x+3y}{3x-y}
=\frac{y+3y}{3y-y}
=\frac{4y}{2y}
=2.
\]
The cancellation is valid because \(y\ne0\). The answer is \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
